notes: Apply every case from a clean state: load dcasimulator/index.html, dismiss any tour overlay, click #resetBtn, then remove every scenario left in #scenarioTabs with #delScenarioBtn until only the scenarios listed in 'scenarios' remain, and click #clearPoolBtn (in #poolChipsWrap) if any asset is already loaded.

'settings' keys are DOM ids on the Settings tab (#randomSeed, #riskFreeRate, #currencySymbol). Set #randomSeed BEFORE creating any simulated asset, because the seed is what makes the synthetic price path reproducible.

'data' describes the Data tab. mode 'simulated': click the 'Simulated' button in #dataModeToggle, then for each entry of 'assets' fill #simNameInput / #simReturnInput / #simStdInput and click #addSimBtn. mode 'real': click 'Real', type the tickers into #tickerPoolInput and click #loadTickersBtn. Then set #startDate and #endDate. Text/number inputs: set .value and dispatch 'input', 'change', 'blur'. Selects: set .value and dispatch 'change'. Checkboxes: click only when the current checked state differs from the requested boolean.

'scenarios' is a list. Create each with #addScenarioBtn and fill the editor that renders into #scenarioConfig, then move to the next with the tabs in #scenarioTabs. The editor is built at runtime, so locate its controls by the visible text of their labels inside #scenarioConfig: 'name' is the scenario name field (or the tab rename control in #scenarioTabs), 'asset' the security/asset selector, 'amount' the contribution amount, 'style' the strategy selector, and 'params' the style-specific controls that appear under it (class .style-params / .param-row).

'style' values are the option values of the strategy selector. Map them by meaning if the value attributes differ: 'monthly' = the plain periodic style that buys on a fixed day of each month; 'weekly' = the plain periodic style that buys on a fixed weekday; 'monthly-top' / 'monthly-bottom' / 'weekly-top' / 'weekly-bottom' = the styles that buy at the highest / lowest close of each month or week; the remaining styles are the conditional ones (technical indicators and price-move rules).

'params' keys and what they mean: day_of_month (day the monthly style buys), weekday, indicator (which technical rule), fast_period, slow_period, rsi_period, threshold_pct (the percentage move a price rule needs), lookback_bars, end_of_period_fallback (the 'buy at the end of the period anyway' checkbox, class .tech-eom), yearly_increase_pct.

Run with #simBtn and wait until #summaryGrid has been rebuilt. Turn on #showAdvancedToggle when Sharpe / Sortino / CAGR are observed. Read: the per-scenario tiles in #summaryGrid, the per-row table in #detailBody after choosing the scenario in #detailSelect, #priceLegend / #equityLegend, #mainWarning, #poolStatus / #simStatus / #dateRangeStatus / #fetchStatus, #rateInfo, and the CSV produced by #downloadBtn.

Report numbers as plain numbers: strip currency symbols and thousands separators, keep the sign, and report a percentage as the number shown (9.7 for '9.7%'). Report text verbatim. Report a quantity that is absent, blank or shown as a dash as null rather than guessing.

Keys whose 'what' begins with 'Runner-computed' are arithmetic the runner performs on other observed values or on the displayed price series (the Price chart's data, or the Price column of the Detailed Breakdown). Compute them from the same values reported for this case; never from anything inside _qa/plan/.
'bar index' means the 0-based position of a date in this scenario's displayed price series after trimming (row 0 of the Detailed Breakdown / the first plotted price point).
Cases with 'states' are several independent states. Apply each from a clean state and prefix that state's observation keys with the state name, exactly as the 'observe' keys are spelled.
A setup carrying "requires": "network" needs the live market-data worker. If it is unreachable, record the case as not-run (an error) rather than substituting anything.
Timezone states: relaunch the browser (or open a new Playwright context) with the named IANA zone - TZ env var or the context's timezoneId - and repeat the whole setup from scratch inside it.

nan_count means: the number of occurrences of 'NaN', 'Infinity', '-Infinity', 'Infinity', 'undefined' or 'null' in the visible text of #summaryGrid, #detailBody and #mainWarning (0 when there are none). js_error_count means the number of uncaught page errors and console errors captured while the case ran.

cases.title: Look-ahead: a signal formed from day D's close cannot be acted on at day D's close

instructions: Run one scenario for EVERY conditional style the strategy selector offers, not only the four sketched above: a conditional style is any style whose purchases depend on a condition computed from price history (technical indicators and percentage-move rules). Keep amount 1000, the same asset and the same window for all of them, and end_of_period_fallback off so only genuine signals buy.

For each purchase, recompute that style's own condition yourself from the displayed close series, using the textbook definition of the rule named in the editor (SMA = mean of the last n closes; EMA = 2/(n+1) smoothing seeded on the first n-bar mean; RSI = Wilder's smoothing; a cross = the bar at which the state changes from false to true; a percentage-move rule = close compared with the stated reference). The 'signal bar' of a purchase is the bar at which the condition that produced it first became true, i.e. the most recent false->true transition at or before the purchase.

observe.what: Number of conditional styles actually run as scenarios in this case.
Total number of purchases across all the conditional scenarios in this case.
Runner-computed: across all the conditional scenarios, the number of purchases whose execution bar index equals the bar index of their own signal bar.
Runner-computed: the number of conditional styles for which sameBar_buy_count is non-zero.
Runner-computed: the smallest value, over every purchase in this case, of (execution bar index - signal bar index).
Runner-computed: the number of purchases whose execution bar index exceeds their signal bar index.
Runner-computed: purchases the runner could not attribute to any signal bar.
See notes.

instructions: Read #rateInfo before touching anything, then create the simulated asset and run the simulation, then read #rateInfo again.
